messages.subject: Re: Markers above threshold not returned
parts:
Ah, I see!  I think part of my confusion was that I am running four phenotypes at once, so I am getting multiple outputs on chromosomes, even though I am only getting the tallest peak per chromosome per phenotype.


I am still a bit confused, though. My plan was to use scanone and scantwo to find QTL that I would put into my model using makeqtl and fitqtl.  The two sources you gave appear to only use the highest LOD score on each chromosome. Since I have multiple QTL on some chromosomes, I was hoping to include them in the model.  

 

So, I should just incorporate the highest peak for each chromosome?  What about in the event that two peaks on the same chromosome are higher and account for more variance than the highest peak on a separate chromosome?  As an example, if I have two distinct peaks on chromosome 3 with each having a LOD score of 7 or more and another, single peak on chromosome 5 at 3.4, then is it still correct to only include the highest peak from each chromosome?


I have also read the MQM Tutorial which uses the locus on each chromosome with the greatest LOD score as a co-factor, but I am interested in the original LOD scores.  Using a marker as a co-factor alters the LOD score in the new analysis.

 

I hope I've explained my confusion accurately.  If not, please let me know.  I'm really just looking for a list of all QTL above a given threshold. Correct me if I am wrong, but I think I can do it manually for my population with 69 markers, find the marker at each cM position, and then finding the confidence interval should also give me the LOD Score at that marker.  I do not think I could do this manually with my sub-population with 578 markers, though. 


Thank you!

 

Miranda

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Markers above threshold not returned
parts:
Except in large crosses, it is usually difficult to obtain good evidence for linked QTL, but I feel it's better to focus on multiple-QTL models than to look at peaks in the scanone results.

The results of scantwo can be quite informative about the possibility of two QTL on a chromosome, and scantwo will give an estimate of the locations of the two QTL, which you can then use in makeqtl() and fitqtl() for exploring larger models. It's up to you whether you want to pick out the single highest peak on a chromosome, or two pick out two peaks on the same chromosome.

You could also form a model containing the loci with major effect and then use addqtl() or addpair() to do a scan for an additional QTL or an additional pair of QTL.

karl
